title: Even-Gap Split Points
statement:
You get an integer array nums. A split point i (with 0 ≤ i < n − 1) cuts the array into a left part nums[0 .. i] and a right part nums[i + 1 .. n − 1]. Both parts are non-empty.

Return how many split points make leftSum − rightSum an even number. Negative differences count too: −4 is even.

examples.why: The differences are 3 − 13 = −10, 8 − 8 = 0 and 10 − 6 = 4. All three are even.
The differences are −3 and 5. Both are odd.
The only split gives 7 − 7 = 0, which is even.

hints: Keep a running left sum; the right sum is total − left. That alone gives an O(n) solution.
Write the difference as left − (total − left) = 2 · left − total. What does 2 · left contribute to its parity?
The difference is even exactly when total is even, no matter where you split. So the answer is n − 1 or 0.

explain.intuition:
The difference at any split is left − (total − left) = 2 · left − total. The 2 · left part is always even, so the parity of the difference is the parity of total. It does not depend on the split at all.

So either every one of the n − 1 split points works (total even) or none does (total odd). A prefix-sum scan gets the same answer and is what you would write before noticing the shortcut; it is worth saying both in an interview.
steps: Compute total, the sum of the array.
pitfalls: Letting the split run up to i = n − 1, which leaves the right part empty. There are only n − 1 valid splits.
Taking % 2 === 1 of a negative difference in JavaScript, which gives -1. Test % 2 === 0 instead, or use the total.
Recomputing both sums from scratch for every split, which is O(n²).

solutions.title: Recompute both sums at every split
solutions.idea: For each split, add up the left and right parts directly and test the difference.

solutions.title: Running prefix sum
solutions.idea: Keep the left sum as you move the split; the right sum is total minus left.

solutions.title: Parity of the total
solutions.idea: The difference is 2 · left − total, so its parity is the parity of total for every split.

followups: Count splits where the difference is divisible by 3 instead. Does the shortcut still work?
Count splits where leftSum ≥ rightSum. Which of the three solutions adapts?
